name: Cross Wm Gamma Beta Dynamics

cross_template_interactions.description: Attention gates what environmental information enters working memory: attended features encoded via gamma oscillations; unattended features remain implicit and don't occupy WM capacity.
Thalamic gating provides pre-filtered sensory streams; WM gamma encoding then selectively represents subset of thalamic-admitted information. Layered filtering: thalamic → attentional → WM.
Proactive control relies on sustained WM maintenance (beta oscillations); reactive control operates on transient gamma encoding. WM dynamics support both control modes.
Architectural complexity determines WM load: complex building floor plans require higher WM capacity (4±1 chunks). Hierarchy level complexity cascades to WM demands.
Environmental stimulus complexity (high-end dose-response) increases WM load. Optimal environmental stimulation matches WM capacity; overload occurs when stimulation exceeds ~5 chunks.
